findings.body:
Removing `@require_role("admin")` leaves `DELETE /users/<user>` with no authorization at all. Any client that can reach the app can delete any user (including admins) and get `204`.

The 403s on cleanup jobs come from `require_role` checking the **path** `user` against `ROLES`, so targets with role `viewer` always fail — that is a broken caller-vs-target check, not a reason to drop the guard.

Restore an access check that authorizes the **caller** (admin session, service account, or scoped API key). If cleanup needs non-interactive delete rights, grant that principal an explicit role and enforce it here before `USERS.remove(user)`.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change removes the only access control on `DELETE /users/<user>`, leaving user deletion fully open to any caller who can reach the endpoint.

## Analysis

`app.py` has a single destructive route and a single guard: `@require_role("admin")`. There is no other authentication middleware, session check, or service-account gate in the codebase. Dropping that decorator means any client can permanently remove entries from `USERS` and receive `204`.

The PR description says cleanup jobs running as the viewer account were getting 403s. That symptom is real under the current decorator shape: `require_role` compares `ROLES.get(user)` where `user` is the **path parameter** (the account being deleted), so deleting `bob` (`viewer`) always 403s while deleting `alice` (`admin`) is allowed. That is broken authorization design, but stripping the decorator is the wrong fix — it trades a confused role check for **unauthenticated destructive access**, including the ability to delete admin users.

## What to do instead

Keep a guard on the route and authorize the **caller** (API key, service role, or admin session), not the target username in the path. If cleanup jobs need a dedicated identity, give them an explicit principal with delete permission and check that principal inside `require_role` / a sibling decorator.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
